name: MonarchAiLauncher
title: AiLauncher
wrapsNative: Button with a custom ButtonStyle and keyboardShortcut(_:); placed by the app with safeAreaInset or overlay
summary: The button that opens and closes an AI assistant: a round floating button or a quieter toolbar button, with an unread dot, a working ring or a count, and a hardware keyboard shortcut.
whenToUse: As the one way into the assistant on a screen: the solid variant in a safeAreaInset or overlay at the bottom trailing corner, the subtle variant in a toolbar or rail.
whenNotToUse: Not for sending a prompt or stopping a reply. Not more than one launcher with a shortcut on a screen.
api: init(isOpen: Binding<Bool>, systemImage: String? = nil, variant: MonarchAiLauncherVariant = .solid, badge: MonarchAiLauncherBadge? = nil, showsLabel: Bool? = nil, shortcut: KeyboardShortcut? = KeyboardShortcut("j", modifiers: .command), label: String? = nil, badgeLabel: String? = nil, openLabel: String? = nil)
enum MonarchAiLauncherBadge { case unread, working, count(Int) }

options.name: isOpen
options.description: Whether the assistant the launcher controls is open. The button toggles it.

options.name: systemImage
options.description: An SF Symbol that replaces the AI glyph.

options.name: variant
options.description: solid is the round, filled, raised floating button; subtle is a tinted button with its label for a toolbar.

options.name: badge
options.description: unread (a dot), working (a ring) or count.

options.name: showsLabel
options.description: Shows the label beside the glyph. nil shows it for the subtle variant only.

options.name: shortcut
options.description: The hardware keyboard shortcut that toggles isOpen. nil for none.

options.name: badgeLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken text of the badge.

options.name: openLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Open" spoken while the assistant is open.

states.name: open
states.description: The solid variant shows a close mark instead of the glyph; the subtle variant gets a stronger border.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With disabled(true): a muted fill and the disabled text role, no AI colour.

states.name: unread
states.description: A dot at the top trailing corner.

states.name: working
states.description: A part of the outline travels around the button. Under Reduce Motion the whole outline is drawn and still.

states.name: count
states.description: The number at the top trailing corner, "99+" above 99, nothing for zero or less.

appearance: solid is filled with the solid AI role with the on-solid role for the glyph and a medium shadow; subtle is the subtle AI fill with the AI border and the strong AI role. The dot and the count are the solid danger role ringed in the surface role; the working ring is the AI thinking role. All roles come from the theme.
platformNotes: The web positions the launcher itself (bottom-end, bottom-start, inline) and moves it above other floating elements with avoidSelector. On iOS the app places it with safeAreaInset or overlay, which is how the system keeps it clear of bars, the keyboard and other insets, so there are no position or avoid parameters; the two looks are the solid and subtle variants. The shortcut is the standard keyboardShortcut, so it works with a hardware keyboard only, is listed by the system when Command is held on iPad, and is not drawn beside the label. It also works while a text field has focus; the web's shortcutInEditable switch has no equivalent. The web puts the badge text in the accessible name; here it is the accessibility value.
accessibility: A button named "Assistant", or the label parameter.
The value is "Open" while the assistant is open, followed by the badge: "New messages", "Working" or the count of unread messages.
The touch target is at least 48 by 48 points for the solid variant and 44 by 44 for the subtle one.
The badge is also spoken, so it does not depend on colour or on the dot alone.
The working ring is still under Reduce Motion. The glyph and the badge are hidden from VoiceOver as separate elements.
The dot and the count sit at the top trailing corner, which mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
edgeCases: A long label wraps; the solid variant then becomes a pill.
The count has one built-in string for one message and one for more; languages with more plural forms need badgeLabel.
The badge stands 4 points outside the button, so leave that much room at the corner.
